hints: Focus on what makes a nitrogen species basic or acidic, and what holds nitrogen atoms together, rather than just memorising names.
Remember that ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$, has a lone pair, but in $\text{NH}_4^+$ that lone pair has already been used to bond to $\text{H}^+$.
Think about which nitrogen oxide helps turn $\text{SO}_2$ into $\text{SO}_3$ in the air and is regenerated, that is the hallmark of a catalyst.
walkthrough:
**Test the ammonium ion claim**

Think simply first. A base needs a lone pair to accept $\text{H}^+$. Ammonia $\text{NH}_3$ has one, so it is basic.

Formation of ammonium:
$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{NH}_4^+$$

**See why ammonium cannot be basic**

Once $\text{NH}_3$ forms $\text{NH}_4^+$, the lone pair is now a bonding pair to the fourth hydrogen. There is no lone pair left to accept another proton.

So $\text{NH}_4^+$ is actually acidic (it can donate $\text{H}^+$), not basic.

**Check the smog and nitrogen reactivity claims**

Peroxyacetyl nitrate, PAN, is itself a product and component of photochemical smog, formed from nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons in sunlight. It is not a reactant that $\text{NO}$ attacks to make smog.

Nitrogen, $\text{N}_2$, is $\text{N} \equiv \text{N}$ with a very strong triple covalent bond. It is non-polar, so there are no permanent dipole attractions at all. Its inertness is due to very high bond energy.

**Confirm the sulfur dioxide oxidation**

In the atmosphere, $\text{NO}_2$ oxidises $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$, which then forms acid rain. The $\text{NO}$ formed is re-oxidised back to $\text{NO}_2$ by oxygen, so $\text{NO}_2$ acts as a catalyst.

Key catalytic cycle:
$$\text{SO}_2 + \text{NO}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_3 + \text{NO}$$
$$\text{NO} + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{NO}_2$$
This is the only correct statement.

options.A: False. Basic character needs an available lone pair. $\text{NH}_3$ has one, but $\text{NH}_4^+$ has used it to form the fourth N-H dative bond, so it has no lone pair left. $\text{NH}_4^+$ is the conjugate acid, not a base.
options.B: False. This reverses the chemistry. Peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN) is itself a harmful secondary pollutant component of photochemical smog, produced involving $\text{NO}_2$, hydrocarbons and sunlight. $\text{NO}$ does not react with PAN to make smog.
options.C: Correct. $\text{NO}_2$ catalyses atmospheric oxidation of $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$. $\text{NO}_2$ is reduced to $\text{NO}$ and then regenerated by oxidation with $\text{O}_2$, so it meets the definition of a catalyst.
options.D: False. $\text{N}_2$ is very unreactive because of the very strong $\text{N} \equiv \text{N}$ triple covalent bond with very high bond energy. $\text{N}_2$ is non-polar with no permanent dipole, so permanent dipole-permanent dipole forces do not exist between the atoms.
